$comment: Language-neutral conformance vectors: pure JSON, no executable content. The JS reference model and the future Rust engine must both pass every vector (MP-7MCP-01 / MP-PAR-01).
contract: mp-7mcp-01 v3 + provider-neutral rollout + cloud quarantine

stepSemantics.patch: RFC 7386 JSON merge patch applied to the live state (null deletes a key; arrays and scalars replace). A vector-level 'patch' is applied to the baseline state before the first step.
stepSemantics.authorizeWrite: Admission decision for the named auth profile and request. expect.code is compared exactly.
stepSemantics.simulateWrite: Admission, atomic commit, receipt and disclosure re-check. State changes persist to later steps (receipts, approvals consumed, write log).
stepSemantics.ownerApprove: The owner approves exactly this request in the trusted local UI: a single-use approval bound to client, vault, collection, operation, operation id, canonical body digest, policy revision and epoch. 'overrides' replaces approval fields (for stale or expired cases).
stepSemantics.canRead: expect.value is true only for an independent read grant on the collection under the current read policy revision; never for a cloud principal on the raw layer.
stepSemantics.validateGrant: Grant issuance check against the named client at the live 'now'. expect.ok and, when not ok, expect.reason.

vectors.title: No grant means DENIED; a write grant never confers read
A grant for another operation or object kind does not authorize
Mode deny, or an absent mode, means DENIED
ask_first needs a server-side owner approval bound to the exact request, consumed once
An approval for one body cannot authorize a different body or operation id
An expired approval, or one from a previous epoch, is not accepted
Delete is a tombstone that always needs approval; tombstoned objects are immutable over MCP
Same operation id and body replays the receipt; a different body is a CONFLICT
update with a stale expectedRevision is a CONFLICT, the current revision is accepted
create_import may not carry a client-chosen object id
Revoking the grant, bumping the epoch, locking, pausing or an unreadable authority store all deny the next call
Editing write policy invalidates older grants
A cloud grant past expiresAt is denied
Local credentials never work through the tunnel; a cloud principal cannot present a local credential class
Raw layer permits only create_import and append, even for a local client
A cloud client is denied raw writes and raw reads even with grants
Cloud writes are confined to the client's own quarantine collection
A cloud move needs grants on source and destination, and the destination must be the client's own quarantine
ChatGPT and Gemini hosted write is DEFERRED: no grant can be issued and an existing credential is denied; one capability model, rollout is credential state
Deferring hosted write does not change curated read for ChatGPT or Gemini
Enabling a provider changes only rollout state; the same operation and grant shape then works; removing the rollout entry fails closed
Cloud per-request object count and per-hour write limits
Cloud grant issuance requires an expiry within the 30-day default cap
Cloud principals cannot hold bulk grants; unknown object kinds are denied
